 :J U D G M E N T:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 11-02-2024 at about 6-50-7.00 am., the petitioner was riding the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 53-HH-4035 on Hirandahalli - Bidarajalli road and when he reached East Point College, near Walnut Interiors, Bidarahalli, Bengaluru, at that time all of a sudden Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-0-Ak-6908 which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner took right turn of the vehicle without giving any indications or putting any indicator, result of which the petitioner dashed against the Auto Rickshaw.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to East Point Hospital,
Benglauru wherein admitted as an inpatient for a period of 6 days and then he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as an inpatient for a period of 50 days.

Thereafter, he was shifted to Surgical Care Hospital, Bengaluru wherein admitted as an inpatient for a period of 1 month and from the said date till this date the petitioner is taking physiotherapy treatment.
The petitioner underwent surgeries and he was discharged from the hospital with an advice to continue the follow up treatment and to undergo periodical review.
So far, the petitioner has spent sum of Rs.75,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was working as a Bus driver at Narayana School, Borigere and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the unfortunate accident, the petitioner is unable to walk, sit, walk, sit and he is in COMA stage.

4. Along with the petition, the petitioner had filed IA no I under Order XXXII Rule 1 and 2 r/w Sec.151 of CPC to appoint his father as the legal guardian and permit the guardian to represent the petitioner.
In pursuance of the application, the petitioner was called to appear before the court so as to hold preliminarily enquiry.
On 01-04-2025 the petitioner has come before the court in wheel chair with the assistance of his father, mother and uncle.

This court had posed many more questions to the petitioner regarding the vehicle number, the date of accident and the place at which accident in question has occurred etc., but the petitioner was not able to recollect the incident and failed to Sandeep H M vs Muniyappa on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35236548/
2 give any answer to the questions posed to him and for what ever the questions asked to him he kept mum.
Further it is so visible that the physical and mental condition of the petitioner appears to be not normal.

In view of the medical evidence given by the PW.2 coupled with the preliminary enquiry conducted by this court, this court had formed opinion that the petitioner is not in a position to give rational answer.
Accordingly permission was granted to represent the petitioner by his father as a next friend.
5. Respondent no.1/

the RC owner of Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-0-Ak-6908 has filed written statement and contended that he is the owner of the Auto Rickshaw and the same was insured with the respondent no.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

The respondent no.1 further contended that on the date of the accident he was driving the Auto Rickshaw carefully by following all the traffic rules and the petitioner by riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner caused the accident.
Hence petitioner alone is responsible for the accident.
The respondent no.1 further stated that at the time of the accident the petitioner was not holding valid driving licence and he was not wearing helmet.

6. Respondent No.2- the insurer of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MM-3266 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence and was not having valid permit as on date of accident and the offending vehicle and that the accident in question has occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner as petitioner by riding the motor cycle in rash and negligent manner hit to the Auto Rickshaw.
7.
On the basis of the above pleadings following Issues were framed.

: I S S U E S:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of Road Traffic Accident on 11.02.2024 at about 6.50 - 7.00 a.m., on Hirandahalli-Bidarahalli road, East Point College, Near Walnut Interiors, Bidarahalli, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-AK-6908 ?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
8. In support of the case of the petitioner, Asha Jyothi A - Medical Record Technician is examined as PW.1 and marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
Dr. Shailesh A V - Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon is examined as PW.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P10 to Ex.P16.

The father/natural guardian of the petitioner is examined as PW.3 and got marked documents as as per Sandeep H M vs Muniyappa on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35236548/
3 Ex.P.17 to 42, 45, 46, 52 and 52(a)/

sentences.text: Mahaboob Pasha- MRO at East Point Hospital is examined as PW.4 and marked documents as per Ex.P43 and Ex.P44 and Lingappa A - HR Manager in Infants Travel Pvt. Ltd., is examined as PW.5 and marked documents as per Ex.P47 to Ex.P51
On the other hand, K S Vishwantha - Branch Manager at HAL ESI Corporation is examined as RW.1 and marked documents as per Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.

The respondent no.1 has examined himself as Rw.2 and marked documents as per Ex.R3 to Ex.R6.
9.
Heard the argument of learned counsel for petitioner and respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record.

10. My findings on the above-referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue no 3: As per the final order, for the following.

:REASONS:
11. Issue no 1: In order to prove the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the father/next friend of the petitioner is examined as PW.3.

The Pw3 has deposed that on 11-02-2024 at about 6-50-7.00 am., the petitioner was riding the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-HH-4035 on Hirandahalli - Bidarajalli road and when he reached East Point College, near Walnut Interiors,
Bidarahalli, Bengaluru, at that time all of a sudden a Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-0-Ak- 6908 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner took right turn of the vehicle without giving any indications or putting any indicator, result of which the petitioner dashed against the Auto Rickshaw.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

12. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.3 has relied upon Ex.P17 to Ex.P27 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint,
police intimation, spot mahazar, photograph of the scene of occurrence, seizer mahazar, notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon, indemnity bond, IMV report, wound certificate,
another notice u/Sec.133 of IMV report and reply given thereon, another indemnity bond, etc.,
13.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by father of the petitioner by name Venkatesh, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 0065/2024 of Avalahalli Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC r/w u/Sec. 122,187 of MV Act.
14.

The learned counsel for respondent no.1 and 2 has vehemently argued that the petitioner is the sole cause for the accident and the petitioner by riding his motor cycle in high speed had lost control over the vehicle, result of which he fell down with motor cycle and that auto rickshaw did not touch the motor cycle and that respondent no.1 has already taken the offending vehicle towards right turn and at that time the petitioner by riding his vehicle in an excessive speed lost control over the vehicle Sandeep H M vs Muniyappa on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35236548/
4 and fall down from the vehicle.
Hence offending vehicle is no way involved in the accident.

15. As observed supra, the PW.1 has refuted the said contention taken by the respondents and to prove that accident in question has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, he has produced the pen-drive and same was marked as Ex.P52.
The said device was exhibited in the open court.
As observed by this court from the device, the respondent no.1 who is the driver of the offending vehicle was driving the vehicle in a straight road.

When he reached the spot, he took his vehicle towards the extreme left side of the road and then took right turn of the vehicle, at that time the petitioner came in a high speed on seeing the offending vehicle taking right turn appears to have applied brake result of which he lost control over the vehicle fell down from the motor cycle.

16. By referring the scene of occurrence depicted in the Ex.P52, the counsel for respondent no.2 has posed question to the PW.1 that the distance between the place at which petitioner was lying and the place at which the offending vehicle was nearly 5 to 10 feet.
The PW.3 has admitted the said suggestion and also admitted that as depicted in the Video clippings at the time of accident, the petitioner was not wearing helmet.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that the driver of the offending vehicle without giving any indication all of a sudden took the vehicle towards right turn result of which this mishap has occurred.
17. If the evidence of the RW.2 who is the driver of the offending vehicle is perused, on the date of accident, the offending vehicle was proceeding from Aavanahalli towards Bidarehalli.

It is admitted by RW.2 that by proceeding from Avanahalli towards Bidarahalli in a straight road, he took his vehicle towards extreme left side of the road, at that time one BMTC bus was passed through the said road.
It is admitted by RW.2 that whenever any person takes U turn of the vehicle, he has to observe whether any vehicles are coming in the said road.

It is deposed by RW.2 that while taking right U turn of the offending vehicle, the vehicle of the petitioner was not coming in the said road and it is after the U turn taken by him, at a distance of nearly 5 to 10 feet from the offending vehicle,
the vehicle of the petitioner fall down.
It is admitted by RW.2 that the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 25 feet and it is two way road and vehicles are moving on both direction of the road.

The RW.2 has deposed that "
     
       .   
        
       
      
    ."

18. The RW.2 by giving evidence to the aforesaid effect has admited that without giving any indication and without observing any vehicular movement in the said road, he abruptly took right turn of the vehicle and without expecting the respondent no.1 taking sudden right turn of the offending vehicle on seeing the offending vehicle taking right turn the petitioner tried to take control over the motor cycle but since petitioner was riding the vehicle at high speed, he could not have Sandeep H M vs Muniyappa on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35236548/
5 control over the motor cycle result of which he fell down and sustained grievous head injuries and other injuries.
19.
The RW.2 during his cross examination has admitted that, before the Jurisdictional Magistrate he has admitted his guilty and deposited the fine amount.

20. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 at this juncture has relied upon the judgment reported in 2014 AIR SCW 1081 between Lachoo Ram and Ors Vs Himachal Road Transport Corpn,. wherein it was observed that "Mere involvement of bus of respondent corporation in accident- cannot make respondent liable to pay compensation unless it is shown that accident was caused by rash and negligent act of bus driver."
21.

entities.text: 2014 AIR SCW 1081 between Lachoo Ram and Ors Vs Himachal Road Transport Corpn
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 531 2023 INSC 621 between Mathew Alexander Vs Mohammed Shafi and Another., it was observed that "while considering a petition for compensation for death or injury in a road accident, the standard of proof to be applied by the motor accident claims Tribunal, is the preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof of beyond reasonable doubt would not apply.

entities.text: Mathew Alexander Vs Mohammed Shafi and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The final report in the Criminal Investigation connected to the accident would not have a bearing on the claim petition and that claim petition must be considered on its own merits."

22. In 2005(3) Supreme 587 Supreme Court of India between National Insurance Co.Ltd Vs Prembai Patel and Ors, it was observed that "the claim petition before the motor accident claim Tribunal is an action in tort and the injured or the legal representatives of the deceased have to establish by preponderance of evidence that there was no negligence on the part of the injured or deceased and they were not responsible for the accident."
23.

sentences.text: Now considering the observation made in the aforesaid rulings coupled with the evidence of RW.1 and the scene of occurrence one depicted in the device which was exhibited before the court it can be gathered that, it is true that the Auto Rickshaw did not touch the motor cycle.
But the mere fact that the offending vehicle did not touch the motor cycle of the petitioner it does not mean that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.

As noticed by this court by watching the scene of occurrence in the device displayed before the court, the respondent no.1 by proceeding from Aavanahalli towards Bidarehalli took his vehicle towards extreme left side of the road and without giving any indication took right U turn of the vehicle and at the same time the petitioner by riding his vehicle in high speed, without expecting the offending vehicle taking right turn, on seeing the offending vehicle in his attempt to apply the brake lost control over the vehicle and fallen from the motor cycle result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Hence the mere fact that the Investigating officer has filed charge sheet only against the respondent no.1 and that respondent no.1 has pleaded guilty before the Magistrate court, this court by relying upon the aforesaid document cannot come to the conclusion that accident in question has occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
It can be said that even the petitioner too has contributed negligence.

So far as percentage of negligence contributed by the petitioner and respondent no.1 is concerned it can be assessed at the ratio of 25:75 because though petitioner was riding the motor cycle in high speed but he was proceeding on the correct side of the road.

When respondent no.1 was taking right turn, he ought to have taken all kind of precautionary measures Sandeep H M vs Muniyappa on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35236548/
6 but as admitted by him without observing the vehicular movement in the road, he took right turn of the vehicle.
Hence the percentage of negligence contributed by the respondent no.1 is on higher side.
Since petitioner has also contributed negligence at the ratio of 25%, he has to forgo compensation to an extent of 25%.
Accordingly issue no.1 is answered in partly affirmative.
24. Issue No.2:- The father/next friend of the petitioner has given evidence to the effect of petitioner/Sandeep H M sustained grievous head injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P2 to Ex.P16, Ex.P28 to Ex.P33 and Ex.P39 to Ex.P42.
On going through the medical documents it reveals that the petitioner has taken treatment at East Point Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient from 11-02-2024 to 17-02-2024.

From there he was shifted to Manipal Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient from 17-02- 2024 to 25-03-2024 and then he was shifted to Surge Care Hospital from 24-03-2024 to 24-04-2024 and again he has taken treatment at Cauvery Hospital from 20-11-2024 to 23-11-2024.
Thus the petitioner has taken treatment in all for a period of 73 days.

As per the wound certificate at Ex.P25, the petitioner has sustained 5 injuries of which injury no.4 and 5 are simple in nature and injury no.1, (a), (b), 2, 3 (a),
(b), (c),
(d), (e), (f) are grievous in nature.

25. Dr. Sahailesh A.V. Rao, Senior consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics is examined as Pw2 and through him OPD records, skull x-ray report, CT brain report, Mini mental stage examination report, Neuro Psychological assessment report and Skull x-ray film and CT scan film are marked as Ex.P10 to Ex.P16.

PW.2 has deposed that petitioner was evaluated by him at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bangalore on 17-02- 2025, 18-02-2025 and again on 25-02-2025 for the purpose of assessing his disability and that the petitioner is unable to attend his earlier work.
He complains of weakness of left side and unable to stand or walk.
He also has decreased memory.

26. It is deposed by PW.2 that on examination it revealed that petitioner was conscious, he was brought on a wheelchair and he was unable to stand or walk, he has weakness on left side with a power of around 1-2/5.
He has impaired memory and has a large bony defect on right side of his head.
27. It is further deposed by PW.2 that Neuro Psychological Assessment was done to the petitioner on 25-02-2025.
He was unable to perform any task.

His IDEA score was 10, suggestive of 40-70%
disability.
His MMSE was done on 18-02-2025 and he obtained a low score 17/30 and that as per the skull x-ray and CT brain showed a large right fronto tempro partietal boney defect.
VP Shunt tubes were seen in situ.
Glotic changes seen in right fronto temporo parietal region.
28. PW.2 has further deposed that he assessed the disability as per the Disability Assessment and Certification Guidelines issued by DGHS, GOI during 2001 and 2018.
He has a neuro disability pertaining to left side weakness and cognition and that the petitioner has sustained permanent disability of whole body at 50%.
The petitioner requires another brain surgery to close his skull defect.

sentences.text: If the evidence of PW.2 is perused, he is not a treated doctor.

It is deposed by PW.2 that at the time of examination of petitioner his GCS level was 15 and that since there is defect in the skull of the petitioner, it requires implanting metallic plate and that since petitioner was not in a position to understand the question posed to him, his IQ level was not assessed.
It was suggested to the PW.2 that since petitioner requires future treatment, on taking future treatment there is possibility of variation in the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner.

The PW.2 denied the said suggestion and deposed that the future treatment required to the petitioner is only to implant metallic plate for protection hence there is no chances of variation in the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner on taking his future treatment.
30. If the entire medical documents with oral evidence of PW.2 is perused, petitioner has sustained severe head injury.
He has incurred medical expenses of more than Rs 36,00,000/- and he has taken treatment as an inpatient for a period of 73 days.
As observed supra PW.2 has assessed the disability of petitioner at 50% on whole body.
At the cost of repetition PW.2 has deposed that since petitioner was not able to give answer to the question posed to him, his IQ level was not assessed by the PW.2.

It is relevant to state here that, while deciding guardian application filed by the petitioner,
preliminary enquiry was conducted by this court under 32 Rule 15 CPC.
On the date of enquiry under order 32 Rule 15 CPC, the petitioner came before the court in a wheel chair with the assistance of his parents.
This court had posed many number of questions to the petitioner but petitioner was not able to give any answer and he failed to recollect the incident.
Further on seeing the petitioner it can be assessed that he is not in normal position both physically and mentally.

Hence by holding that petitioner is not in a position to represent the case independently, his father/guardian was permitted to represent the petitioner and accordingly the guardian of the petitioner prosecuted the case.

The learned counsel for respondent no.2 during the course of argument has submitted that petitioner is mentally sound and he himself has given reply to the notice issued under Section 133 IMV Act and he himself has executed the indemnity bond and himself has given statement under Section 161 of Cr.PC.

But if the reply notice as per Ex.P26 and indemnity bond as per Ex.P27 is perused it is the brother of the petitioner who has given reply to the notice under Section 133 IMV Act and it is the brother of the petitioner who has executed indemnity bond and got the motor cycle released in their favour.
It is true that the charge sheet contains the statement alleged to be given by the petitioner but the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.PC does not bear the signature of the petitioner.
As per the medical records the petitioner was in unconscious state of mind at the time of his taking treatment.

Hence there is no reason to believe that the petitioner has given statement under Section 161 of Cr.PC.
31.
From the materials placed on record it can be gathered that petitioner is driver by profession.
The respondents have not seriously disputed the avocation of the petitioner as driver by profession.
32. In a ruling reported in 2023 ACJ 490 between Manjunath / Sunil and Another, the injured aged about 27 years suffered brain hemorrhage with damaged frontal and temporal lobes affecting his memory.
Tribunal in absence of evidence of doctor regarding disability suffered by the injured awarded certain sum towards medical expenses and pain and agony.

The injured was examined by a doctor pursuant to an order of appellate court who opined that insured's memory is decreasing he is unable to do any work and assessed permanent disability at 50 percent.

Appellant court taking in to Sandeep H M vs Muniyappa on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35236548/
8 consideration the notional income of the petitioner added 40 percent of income towards future prospects adopted multiplier 18, considering that injured cannot do any work assessed functional disability of 100 percent.

sentences.text: 33. Coming to the case in hand since petitioner was driver by profession and when petitioner is not in a position to do any work because of his mental condition, even though PW.3 had assessed the disability at 50% on whole body, but by considering that the petitioner cannot do any work, it is just to assess the functional disability at 100%.

Considering the seriousness of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the physical and mental condition of the petitioner, this court would consider the disability suffered by the petitioner at 100%.
34. Hence considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
35. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained three grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards pain and suffering.

36. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the Next friend of the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 320 medical bills for Rs.36,80,163/- and 14 medical for Rs.65,036/- as per Ex.P33 and Ex.P39.

IF the cross examination of PW.3 by the learned counsel for respondents is perused it is true that the counsel for respondent no.2 has posed suggestion that PW.3 has not paid the medical bills and that the petitioner has not produced related medical bills to the medical prescription produced by him but they have not seriously disputed the genuineness of the medical bills.
As observed supra, the petitioner has produced abundant medical bills for the long treatment taken by him.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation for Rs.37,45,036/- under the medical expenses.

37. It is stated that petitioner was aged about 24 years and he was bus driver at Narayana School,
Borigere and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
The petitioner has produced statement of account as per Ex.P38 and salary slip as per Ex.P46.
The petitioner has examined HR Manager in Infants Travel Pvt. Ltd., as PW.5 and through him salary slip, driver Data Form, ESI card, notice period information are marked as per Ex.P47 to Ex.P51.

The documents as per Ex.P47 to Ex.P51 produced by the PW.5 coupled with Ex.P38 and the oral evidence of PW.5 clearly proves that the petitioner was working as driver at Narayana School and was drawing monthly salary of Rs.17,170/-.
Hence the monthly income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.17,170/-.
Further as per Ex.P51 i.e., notice period information, the petitioner was relieved from service on 10.02.2024 because of the injuries sustained in the accident.

38. When percentage of functional disability of petitioner is taken as 100% and court proceeds to award compensation under the head loss of future income by considering the functional disability of petitioner at 100% under such circumstances the question of awarding compensation under the head loss of income during laid down period does not arise.

sentences.text: From the evidence of Pw3 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at East Point Hospital, Manipal Hospital, Surgical Care Hospital and Cauvery Hospital as an inpatient for a period of 73 days.
as an inpatient.

He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.1,00,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
40. The petitioner has contended that he is aged about 24 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P35/Aadhar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 20-12-2000.
It means the petitioner was aged about 24 years at the time of accident.

41. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.17,170/- p.m. to this amount future prospect of 40% will have to be added which would result in the monthly income of petitioner at Rs.24,038/-.
When the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 24 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is '18'.

So by applying the multiplier '18' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.24,038 x 12 x 100% x1 8 = 51,92,208/- Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.51,92,208/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
42. PW.2 has stated that petitioner requires another brain surgery to close his skull defect.
The PW.2 has not stated the estimated cost of future surgery and has not given estimation.

Hence, this court inclines to award future medical expenses only to the tune of Rs.50,000/-.
43.
The petitioner at his age of 24 years has suffered grievous injuries.
Hence taking in to consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomforts and loss of marriage prospect.

Thus petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.93,87,244/- (Rupees Ninety Three Lakhs Eighty Seven Thousand Two Hundred Forty Four only).
44. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Since both petitioner and respondent no.2 had contributed negligence to the extent of 25:75 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 25%.
The respondent no 2 being the insurer is liable to pay 75% of the awarded compensation to the petitioner.
75% of the compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
accordingly issue no 2 is answered.
45. Issue No.3: In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.93,87,244/- (Rupees Ninety Three Lakhs Eighty Seven Thousand Two Hundred Forty Four only).

The Respondent No 2 is liable to pay 75% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.70,40,433/- +
cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No. II, in all sum of Rs.70,41,433/- (Rupees Seventy Lakhs Forty One Thousand Four Hundred Thirty Three only) with interest on sum of Rs.69,90,433/- at 6% pa., within 2 months from the date of this award.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
the RC owner of Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-0-Ak-6908 has filed written statement and contended that he is the owner of the Auto Rickshaw and the same was insured with the respondent no.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence and was not having valid permit as on date of accident and the offending vehicle and that the accident in question has occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner as petitioner by riding the motor cycle in rash and negligent manner hit to the Auto Rickshaw.
7.

1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of Road Traffic Accident on 11.02.2024 at about 6.50 - 7.00 a.m., on Hirandahalli-Bidarahalli road, East Point College, Near Walnut Interiors, Bidarahalli, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-AK-6908 ?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation?
If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
:REASONS:
11. Issue no 1: In order to prove the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the father/next friend of the petitioner is examined as PW.3.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the basis of the complaint lodged by father of the petitioner by name Venkatesh, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 0065/2024 of Avalahalli Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC r/w u/Sec. 122,187 of MV Act.
14.
The said device was exhibited in the open court.
When he reached the spot, he took his vehicle towards the extreme left side of the road and then took right turn of the vehicle, at that time the petitioner came in a high speed on seeing the offending vehicle taking right turn appears to have applied brake result of which he lost control over the vehicle fell down from the motor cycle.
22. In 2005(3) Supreme 587 Supreme Court of India between National Insurance Co.Ltd Vs Prembai Patel and Ors, it was observed that "the claim petition before the motor accident claim Tribunal is an action in tort and the injured or the legal representatives of the deceased have to establish by preponderance of evidence that there was no negligence on the part of the injured or deceased and they were not responsible for the accident."
23.
But the mere fact that the offending vehicle did not touch the motor cycle of the petitioner it does not mean that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.
As noticed by this court by watching the scene of occurrence in the device displayed before the court, the respondent no.1 by proceeding from Aavanahalli towards Bidarehalli took his vehicle towards extreme left side of the road and without giving any indication took right U turn of the vehicle and at the same time the petitioner by riding his vehicle in high speed, without expecting the offending vehicle taking right turn, on seeing the offending vehicle in his attempt to apply the brake lost control over the vehicle and fallen from the motor cycle result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Hence the mere fact that the Investigating officer has filed charge sheet only against the respondent no.1 and that respondent no.1 has pleaded guilty before the Magistrate court, this court by relying upon the aforesaid document cannot come to the conclusion that accident in question has occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
It can be said that even the petitioner too has contributed negligence.
So far as percentage of negligence contributed by the petitioner and respondent no.1 is concerned it can be assessed at the ratio of 25:75 because though petitioner was riding the motor cycle in high speed but he was proceeding on the correct side of the road.
When respondent no.1 was taking right turn, he ought to have taken all kind of precautionary measures Sandeep H M vs Muniyappa on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35236548/
6 but as admitted by him without observing the vehicular movement in the road, he took right turn of the vehicle.
Further on seeing the petitioner it can be assessed that he is not in normal position both physically and mentally.
Hence by holding that petitioner is not in a position to represent the case independently, his father/guardian was permitted to represent the petitioner and accordingly the guardian of the petitioner prosecuted the case.
But if the reply notice as per Ex.P26 and indemnity bond as per Ex.P27 is perused it is the brother of the petitioner who has given reply to the notice under Section 133 IMV Act and it is the brother of the petitioner who has executed indemnity bond and got the motor cycle released in their favour.
It is true that the charge sheet contains the statement alleged to be given by the petitioner but the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.PC does not bear the signature of the petitioner.
As per the medical records the petitioner was in unconscious state of mind at the time of his taking treatment.
Hence there is no reason to believe that the petitioner has given statement under Section 161 of Cr.PC.
31.
From the materials placed on record it can be gathered that petitioner is driver by profession.
The respondents have not seriously disputed the avocation of the petitioner as driver by profession.
Considering the seriousness of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the physical and mental condition of the petitioner, this court would consider the disability suffered by the petitioner at 100%.
Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards pain and suffering.
38. When percentage of functional disability of petitioner is taken as 100% and court proceeds to award compensation under the head loss of future income by considering the functional disability of petitioner at 100% under such circumstances the question of awarding compensation under the head loss of income during laid down period does not arise.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.
